bridge: Builds on D05 evidence/provenance and S01 threat models. Watch the assigned Fundamentals playlist before the CTI modules.
teaching:
A behaviour map gives investigators shared names for what happened. In ATT&CK a tactic is the goal (why), a technique is a general method (how), and a procedure is a specific use of that method. A domain name or file hash is an indicator, not the behaviour itself. Legitimate administrators can use the same commands, so a mapping does not by itself establish malicious intent.

Work in three columns: observation, interpretation and mapping. First quote the event or report passage. Next explain exactly what it supports and a plausible alternative. Only then select a technique whose definition matches, recording the technique ID, definition version/date, source and uncertainty. Do not add every technique associated with a tool merely because its name appears.

Worked mapping: in a fictional incident, event E2 records process command line ipconfig /all on host H at 09:01 UTC. That command displays network configuration. The current MITRE T1016 definition includes network-configuration discovery using utilities such as ipconfig, so T1016 (System Network Configuration Discovery), under Discovery, is a supported behaviour description. E2 alone does not identify an attacker, prove exfiltration, or exclude routine troubleshooting. If a log gives only a file read with no content or incident context, do not force a more specific mapping.

Version matters. The provider CTI exercises use historical ATT&CK snapshots; compare their answers to those snapshots before applying current definitions. MITRE’s v18 update in October 2025 deprecated the Data Sources object category and introduced Detection Strategies and Analytics with updated Data Components. This changes how defensive knowledge is organised, not whether logs are needed. The current Enterprise tactics page checked on 31 October 2026 includes Stealth and Defense Impairment; older video counts are historical.

A coverage claim needs more than a coloured matrix. State the observed variant, required telemetry and actual validation limits. The Pyramid of Pain is a heuristic about the effort involved in changing indicators, not a universal measure of security value. A sensor name such as Sysmon does not prove a shell was used; a renamed archive does not prove it left the system. Keep source evidence, interpretation and confidence separate and ask what additional evidence would change the conclusion.
example:
Synthetic note
Observation: source event E1 records process X reading file F at 09:00 UTC.
Interpretation: file access occurred under the recorded identity.
Not established: malicious intent, tool family, data exfiltration.
Candidate mapping: only after behaviour meets the selected technique definition.
Record: ATT&CK version, definition link, evidence IDs and uncertainty.
explanation: This deliberately weak observation demonstrates restraint. Mapping a file read to a specific adversary technique without supporting context can overstate the evidence. Conversely, uncertainty should be documented rather than replacing all analysis with a vague label.
exercise: For E1 in the supplied note, fill observed/inferred/unknown columns. Then use the complete E2 case taught in Learn: ipconfig /all on host H at 09:01 UTC. Write a mapping with evidence id, behaviour, technique id/name, definition source/date and one benign alternative. Use https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1016/ as the definition reference. The provider handout is optional additional practice; no command execution is needed.
solution: E1: observed file read under the recorded identity; interpretation limited to that read; unknown intent, human actor, tool family and transfer contents. A specific adversary technique is not established. E2: cite the exact command line and host/time, describe network-configuration discovery, map cautiously to T1016 System Network Configuration Discovery and record the definition version/date you consult (version 1.7, modified 12 May 2026 when checked on 31 October 2026). Routine troubleshooting is a benign alternative. No actor or exfiltration attribution follows from either event.
challenge: For a fresh fictional report “X ran on host H; a log confirms an outbound connection, but no content capture exists,” state what is observed and what would be needed to assert data exfiltration. Propose a cautious mapping workflow.
challenge_solution: Process execution and a connection are observations under the stated logs. Exfiltration requires evidence of data movement/context beyond mere connectivity. Consult the current technique definition, cite evidence, mark confidence and identify missing telemetry.
